--- CRITICAL FINDINGS ---

[DB-1] Prisma client creates new connections in production
File: src/lib/prisma.ts (L1-L40)
Evidence: The code only caches the PrismaClient to globalThis when NODE_ENV !== "production" and otherwise constructs new PrismaClient() on import, which in serverless or edge deployments spawns many DB connections.  
Impact: Connection pool exhaustion (and then 500s) under moderate concurrency (tens–low hundreds of concurrent invocations); breaks at ~10x QPS via connection limits.  
Fix: Use a production-safe singleton (assign to globalThis even in production) or use a pooled DB proxy (PgBouncer) and set small pool limits.

[DB-2] Coupon decrement and order item mutations are not transactional / sequential N+1 writes
File: src/app/api/checkout/create-order/route.ts (L1-L260)
Evidence: coupon quantity is updated via a standalone prisma.coupon.update before order creation, and the "existingOrder" branch runs multiple sequential awaits inside for-loops to update/create/delete order items (per-item update/create/delete).  
Impact: Race conditions that overspend limited coupons and partial/ inconsistent order state plus many DB roundtrips causing high DB CPU/IOPS and latency at scale (fails quickly under concurrent checkout QPS).  
Fix: Wrap coupon validation+decrement and order create/update + item mutations in a single transaction; replace per-item sequential awaits with batched operations (createMany/updateMany/deleteMany or collect promises and execute safely inside tx).

--- CRITICAL FINDINGS ---

[DB-1] Prisma client creates new connections in production
File: src/lib/prisma.ts (L1-L40)
Evidence: The code only caches the PrismaClient to globalThis when NODE_ENV !== "production" and otherwise constructs new PrismaClient() on import, which in serverless or edge deployments spawns many DB connections.  
Impact: Connection pool exhaustion (and then 500s) under moderate concurrency (tens–low hundreds of concurrent invocations); breaks at ~10x QPS via connection limits.  
Fix: Use a production-safe singleton (assign to globalThis even in production) or use a pooled DB proxy (PgBouncer) and set small pool limits.

[DB-2] Coupon decrement and order item mutations are not transactional / sequential N+1 writes
File: src/app/api/checkout/create-order/route.ts (L1-L260)
Evidence: coupon quantity is updated via a standalone prisma.coupon.update before order creation, and the "existingOrder" branch runs multiple sequential awaits inside for-loops to update/create/delete order items (per-item update/create/delete).  
Impact: Race conditions that overspend limited coupons and partial/ inconsistent order state plus many DB roundtrips causing high DB CPU/IOPS and latency at scale (fails quickly under concurrent checkout QPS).  
Fix: Wrap coupon validation+decrement and order create/update + item mutations in a single transaction; replace per-item sequential awaits with batched operations (createMany/updateMany/deleteMany or collect promises and execute safely inside tx).

[DB-3] Order confirmation decrements stock without availability checks
File: src/app/api/checkout/confirm-order/route.ts (L1-L200)
Evidence: confirm-order and verify-payment both load order then run a tx that updates order.status and issues decrement operations on product/productColor.stock with no check for current stock or check+fail.  
Impact: Data inconsistency / oversell under concurrent confirmations for the same SKU (many concurrent purchases can drive stock negative); financial/inventory corruption at modest concurrent rates.  
Fix: Check stock before decrement (SELECT ... FOR UPDATE or conditional update with WHERE stock >= quantity) inside the same transaction and fail/compensate if insufficient.

--- WARNING FINDINGS ---

[DB-4] Unbounded product & category listing queries (no pagination)
File: src/app/api/products/route.ts (L1-L150)
Evidence: GET /api/products uses prisma.product.findMany({ include:..., orderBy:... }) with no skip/take/cursor or server-side pagination; category route similarly returns all matching rows.  
Impact: Query latency and DB CPU/IOPS will spike as products grow (table scans / large result transport); will degrade UX and increase DB cost under high read QPS.  
Fix: Add server-side pagination/cursor-based endpoints (take/skip or cursor) and limit include depth; return lightweight projections.

[DB-5] Missing indexes on common filter/join columns
File: prisma/schema.prisma (L1-L200)
Evidence: Filters use product.category, product.isActive, product.price/stock ranges, review.productId, order.userId/couponId and searches on customerEmail/phone, but schema lacks @@index declarations on these non-unique FK/filter columns.  
Impact: Table scans on large tables -> query latency and DB CPU increases as rows cross ~100k, especially for category filtering and admin searches.  
Fix: Add targeted indexes (e.g., @@index([category, isActive, createdAt]), index on product.price if ranged, index review.productId, index order.userId/couponId, and text indexes where full-text search is needed).

--- INFO ---

[DB-6] Cart and cart-item handlers do sensible batching/transactions
File: src/app/api/cart/route.ts and src/app/api/cart/items/route.ts (L1-L220)
Evidence: Cart GET batches product fetch with one findMany for productIds; cart item mutations use prisma.$transaction to keep cart totals consistent.
